Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaMed Devices Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, CEO; Sarah Kline, CFO; Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. NovaMed Devices demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:
1. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
2. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
3. Hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates
4. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
5. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
6. Competitive dynamics and market share trends
7. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Reynolds will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. We've delivered meaningful efficiency gains here that directly supported our adjusted operating margin expansion of 210 basis points year-over-year to 28.4%. In a medical devices industry facing persistent inflationary pressures on raw materials like titanium alloys for orthopedic implants and nitinol for cardiovascular stents, as well as regulatory headwinds from evolving MDR requirements in Europe, our disciplined approach to SG&A has been a key differentiator.

The headline numbers show Q2 SG&A at $428 million, up just 4% year-over-year on 9% constant-currency revenue growth, driving leverage of over 500 basis points as a percentage of sales—from 32.8% to 27.6%. For the first half of the year, SG&A totaled $842 million, or 28.1% of revenue, a 140 basis point improvement versus H1 last year. This marks the fourth straight quarter of sequential SG&A-to-sales deleveraging, even as we ramped investments in our high-growth structural heart portfolio, including next-gen TAVR valves similar to Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform, and our da Vinci-inspired robotic-assisted surgery systems.

On the selling expense side, which is about 55% of total SG&A, we achieved $22 million in year-over-year savings through a multi-pronged productivity initiative. Key was our rollout of AI-powered CRM tools, integrated with Salesforce Einstein and our proprietary predictive analytics engine, which optimized our 4,500-person field sales force. This reduced time spent on non-value-add administrative tasks by 25%, allowing reps to focus on high-potential procedures like transcatheter mitral valve repairs—where we've seen attach rates climb to 42% in U.S. cath labs. We also consolidated our U.S. regional sales hubs from 18 to 12, capturing $15 million in facility and travel synergies without impacting coverage in key IDNs like HCA Healthcare or Kaiser Permanente.

General and administrative expenses, at 45% of the total, saw even stronger control, flat year-over-year at $192 million despite a 7% rise in headcount to support our U.S. manufacturing expansion for insulin delivery pumps amid the GLP-1 boom. Efficiency gains stemmed from our global shared services center in Bangalore, now handling 70% of back-office functions like procurement and AP/AR—delivering $18 million in savings via robotic process automation from UiPath. We applied zero-based budgeting across G&A categories, scrutinizing every line item; for instance, professional fees dropped 12% through competitive RFPs for FDA 510(k) consulting, avoiding the cost overruns we've seen peers like Integer Holdings face.

Regionally, this played out differently but consistently. In the U.S., our largest market at 52% of revenue, SG&A deleveraged 280 basis points to 26.2% thanks to optimized reimbursement support for our neuromodulation devices, such as spinal cord stimulators competing with Abbott's Proclaim platform. We navigated CMS pricing scrutiny on pass-through payments by streamlining our prior-auth teams with natural language processing AI, cutting processing time by 40%. In Europe, SG&A as a percent of sales improved 190 basis points to 30.1%, despite IFU reprint costs from MDR transitions—our proactive digitization of labeling via Veeva Vault saved €12 million, positioning us ahead of Boston Scientific's challenges in the region. Asia-Pacific was the star, with 360 basis points of leverage to 24.8%, fueled by localized sales enablement in China for our endoscopy portfolio; we shifted 30% of promo budgets to digital key opinion leader engagement on WeChat, mirroring Intuitive Surgical's playbook, which boosted procedure volumes without proportional selling cost inflation.

Strategically, these gains aren't just cost-cutting—they're reinvestment fuel. We've redirected 60% of the $40 million in Q2 efficiencies back into R&D for our bioresorbable scaffolds and digital surgery platforms, targeting the $15 billion structural heart TAM growing at 12% CAGR per Grand View Research. Compared to industry peers, our SG&A-to-sales ratio now sits at the lower end of the large-cap med device spectrum—below Stryker's 28% but ahead of Medtronic's 30%—reflecting our 'grow profitably' ethos amid supply chain normalization and softening elective procedure backlogs.

Looking forward, we expect full-year SG&A to be 27.5% to 28.0% of revenue, implying another $80 million in absolute efficiencies. This assumes continued RPA scaling and no major forex volatility, with upside from our clinician portal adoption, which has already reduced field service calls by 18% for our imaging systems. We're confident this positions us to outperform in a market where value-based care pressures, like those from the CMS Innovation Center's bundled payments for orthopedics, reward lean operators.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography. This came in at 8.2% year-over-year on a constant currency basis—solid performance amid a dynamic macro environment in the medtech space. This marks our sixth straight quarter of accelerating organic growth, up from 6.9% in Q2 2023 and 7.5% in Q1 this year. Excluding the impacts of our recent tuck-in acquisition of NeuroStim Dynamics and favorable FX tailwinds, this reflects the underlying strength of our core franchises: procedural volume recovery, favorable product mix shifts toward higher-acuity devices, modest average selling price expansion in select segments, and recurring revenue from our growing installed base of capital equipment.

Our five key reporting segments—Cardiovascular, Orthopedics, Neuromodulation & Chronic Pain, Diabetes Management, and Endoscopy & Surgical—collectively represent 98% of our portfolio. All figures are organic, constant FX, YoY unless noted otherwise.

Starting with Cardiovascular, our largest segment at 32% of total revenue, we delivered 10.1% organic growth, beating our internal guide of 8-9%. Structural heart remains the star here, with 14% growth driven by strong adoption of our NovaFlow TAVR valve, which captured 12% U.S. market share in the first half, up from 9% a year ago—gaining ground on Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform through superior hemodynamic performance and our streamlined delivery system. Pacemaker and ICD volumes grew 9%, bolstered by our AI-enabled RhythmSync CRM platform, which now integrates real-time analytics to reduce inappropriate shocks by 25%, per our PROSPECT-IV trial data. We saw a 2% ASP lift from premium mix, offset slightly by reimbursement headwinds in Europe. Recurring leads and sensors contributed 42% of segment revenue, up 300 bps YoY.

Orthopedics clocked in at 7.8% organic growth, aligning with expectations. Hip and knee reconstruction drove 9% procedural growth in the U.S., fueled by pent-up elective demand and our next-gen ActiveJoint cementless implants, which feature porous titanium coatings for 20% faster osseointegration—early registry data shows revision rates under 1% at two years, competitive with Stryker's Triathlon. Sports medicine lagged at 4% due to softer meniscus repair volumes amid economic caution, but our BioScaffold ACL augmentation system is ramping, with Q3 launches in APAC. ASPs held flat as value-based bundled payments pressured margins, but our focus on outpatient ASC shifts yielded 15% growth in ambulatory revenue.

Neuromodulation & Chronic Pain was a standout at 12.5% organic growth, our fastest-growing segment. Spinal cord stimulators surged 16%, propelled by the FDA approval and EU CE mark for our PrecisionPulse HF10 therapy, which demonstrated 85% pain relief at 24 months in the SENZA-RCT study—outpacing Abbott's Proclaim. Deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's grew 10%, with installed base expansion via our NeuroGuide directional leads. U.S. reimbursement tailwinds from CMS's new DRG add-ons added 150 bps to growth, while recurring revenue from rechargeables hit 55% of segment sales.

Diabetes Management grew 9.3% organically, with continuous glucose monitors leading at 13% thanks to our VitalSense Pro sensor, now integrated with Apple Health and compatible with Dexcom G7 workflows—U.S. prescriptions rose 18% amid GLP-1 combo therapy tailwinds. Insulin pump attach rates improved to 28% from 25%, driven by our tubeless InfinityPod. However, ASP compression from competitive pricing—Dexcom and Tandem are aggressive—capped upside. Hybrid closed-loop algorithms remain a key differentiator.

Finally, Endoscopy & Surgical delivered 6.4% growth, tempered by supply chain normalization. Robotic-assisted endoscopy grew 11% with our FlexiScope single-use endoscope, reducing infection risks by 40% versus reusables like Boston Scientific's SpyGlass. General surgery robotics lagged at 3% due to Intuitive Surgical dominance, but our OR1 integrated platform gained traction in hybrid ORs, with 20% attach rates for disposables.

Geographically, our growth was balanced but regionally differentiated. In the Americas—75% of revenue—we posted 9.5% organic growth. The U.S., at 68% of total, drove this with 10.2% expansion, reflecting robust elective procedural recovery (up 12% industry-wide per DARVO data) and our 150 bps market share gain to 14% overall. ASC penetration hit 35% in orthopedics and endoscopy, ahead of peers like Zimmer Biomet. Canada and LATAM added 5%, with Brazil's elective rebound post-COVID.

EMEA grew 5.1% organically, or 7% excluding Germany pricing reforms. U.K. and France were bright spots at 8-9%, buoyed by NHS framework wins for TAVR and neuromodulation. Italy's value-based procurement favored our cost-efficient diabetes portfolio, but Germany's DRG cuts shaved 200 bps—mirroring challenges at Medtronic and Becton Dickinson.

Asia-Pacific accelerated to 11.8% growth, our growth engine. China rebounded to 14% despite anti-corruption scrutiny, with Class III approvals for NovaFlow TAVR and CGMs unlocking tier-2 hospitals. Japan grew 10% on SCS reimbursement expansion, while India and SEA delivered 15% via greenfield distributor ramps and affordable orthopedics like our ValueKnee system, tailored for high-volume public hospitals.

Rest of World rounded out at 7.2%, led by Middle East elective surges.

Underpinning this is a favorable mix shift: high-acuity structural heart and neuromodulation now 28% of revenue, up 400 bps YoY, contributing 60% of growth. Recurring revenue—disposables, sensors, service—reached 52% of total, up from 48%, insulating us from capital budget volatility. Installed base grew 9%, with 85% utilization rates.

We're investing $450 million in R&D this year—12% of sales—focusing on AI/ML for predictive analytics (e.g., our HeartAI for arrhythmia forecasting, partnering with Google Cloud) and next-gen robotics with haptic feedback to challenge Intuitive's da Vinci monopoly. We're pursuing 4-5% market share gains annually through clinical superiority, as evidenced by our 15 NEJM publications this half.

Challenges persist: U.S. GLP-1 obesity wave could disrupt diabetes attach rates short-term, and Europe's HTA scrutiny demands more real-world evidence. But tailwinds like aging demographics (global over-65 population up 3% YoY), minimally invasive procedure shifts (CAGR 6% per Evaluate MedTech), and U.S. IRA-driven domestic manufacturing ($200M capex committed) position us well.

Looking forward, we guide Q3 organic growth of 8-10%, with FY24 at 8.5-9.5%. This assumes stable FX, no major M&A, and continued procedural strength.

Moving on to hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates, which remain a key leading indicator for our procedural growth and recurring revenue streams. Adoption here refers to the percentage of our addressable footprint—approximately 4,800 high-volume hospitals and 7,200 ASCs across our core U.S. and select international markets—where we've secured active utilization of our flagship portfolio, including our PrecisionNav robotic navigation system, EndoFlex single-use endoscopes, and OrthoCore joint reconstruction implants.

Overall adoption across both channels hit 42%, up 580 basis points year-over-year and 210 basis points sequentially. Breaking it out: hospital adoption stands at 51%, reflecting a robust 720 bps YOY increase, while ASC adoption accelerated to 28%, up a market-leading 1,040 bps YOY. These gains outpaced the broader MedTech peer set—for context, Intuitive Surgical reported da Vinci system attach rates hovering around 35-40% in similar high-acuity orthopedics and general surgery segments last quarter, and Stryker's Mako robotics adoption in joints is tracking sub-30% in ASCs per their latest filings.

Driving this momentum are several structural tailwinds. First, hospital procedure volumes rebounded 12% YOY, per our same-facility sales data, fueled by pent-up elective demand and a 15% uptick in outpatient migration under CMS's site-neutral payment policies. We've captured 65% market share in navigation-enabled knee procedures among top-quartile hospitals, thanks to our FDA-cleared PrecisionNav 2.0 upgrade, which integrates AI-driven soft-tissue mapping—reducing OR times by 22% in our pivotal trials and boosting surgeon NPS scores to 92.

In ASCs, this channel now represents 28% of our total procedural volume, up from 22% a year ago, aligning with iData Research's forecast of a 14% CAGR through 2028 as ASCs capture 55% of U.S. musculoskeletal procedures by decade's end. Our ASC adoption surge stems from tailored capital-light bundles: for instance, our EndoFlex disposable scopes achieved 35% penetration in GI-focused ASCs, with average case attach rates hitting 4.2 units per procedure—well above the 3.0 industry benchmark—delivering $1,200 in recurring revenue per case at ASPs holding firm at 102% of list.

Regionally, U.S. adoption leads at 48%, buoyed by our 25% sales force expansion into the Southeast and Midwest, where we're converting 18% of greenfield ASC builds. Europe clocked in at 32%, with double-digit gains in Germany's DRG-optimized markets post our CE Mark for OrthoCore's cementless stems; reimbursement tailwinds there added 300 bps to Q3 uptake. APAC remains nascent at 15% but grew 50% YOY, anchored by partnerships with 12 Ping An Good Doctor ASC networks in China, where we're piloting PrecisionNav amid a 20% procedural boom.

Strategically, we're leaning into three initiatives to sustain 1,000+ bps annual adoption expansion. One, evidence generation: our PROSPECT registry now enrolls 5,200 patients across 450 sites, demonstrating 18% lower readmissions versus legacy systems like Zimmer Biomet's ROSA, which should unlock further GPO contracts. Two, freemium-to-premium funneling: 40% of our ASC pilots convert within 90 days via our disposable razor-blade model, mirroring Medtronic's Hugo RAS playbook. Three, M&A adjacency: the recent $450M acquisition of FlexiScope bolsters our single-use endoscopy attach rates to 45% in target ASCs, with synergies projecting $80M in incremental 2025 revenue.

Looking forward, we guide to 45-47% blended adoption by year-end, implying 22% procedural growth and 28% consumables uplift. This positions us to gain 200 bps of ortho market share in 2024, even as hospital margins compress under 2.5% EBITDA pressures from labor and supply chain headwinds.

Next, capital equipment vs consumables mix trends. This continues to be a cornerstone of our high-margin, recurring revenue model. Capital equipment—like our flagship Horizon robotic-assisted surgery systems and Precision Imaging suites—serves as the essential gateway to our annuity-like consumables stream, including single-use endoscopes, disposable ablation catheters, and our proprietary BioFlex implant kits. This razor-blade dynamic mirrors what you've seen at peers like Intuitive Surgical with da Vinci or Stryker's Mako platforms, but we've optimized it further through our ecosystem lock-in strategies.

Total revenue came in at $1.28 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a constant-currency basis. Capital equipment represented 24% of total revenue, or $308 million, up 6% YoY. This was driven by 12% growth in new system placements, particularly our next-gen Horizon R3 robots, where we placed 185 units globally—exceeding our internal target by 8%. ASPs held steady at around $1.7 million per system, reflecting disciplined pricing amid inflationary pressures on semiconductors and precision components.

Consumables made up the lion's share at 76%, or $972 million, surging 17% YoY reported and 19% on a constant-currency basis. Utilization rates on our installed base hit a record 92 procedures per Horizon system annually, up from 87 last year, fueled by our AI-enhanced procedure optimization software that we've rolled out via over-the-air updates.

This mix shift—consumables now at a multi-year high of 76% versus 72% in Q2 of last year—underscores the resiliency of our model. Our trailing 12-month consumables mix stands at 74%, putting us ahead of the industry average of around 65-70% for large-cap medtech peers.

Zooming out to the half-year picture, H1 consumables growth of 18% outpaced capital's 8%, reflecting three core trends. First, installed base expansion and utilization ramp: our global Horizon installed base now exceeds 4,200 systems, up 22% YoY, creating a $2.8 billion addressable consumables TAM just from robotics alone. Utilization has benefited from pent-up elective procedure demand post-COVID, with orthopedics and structural heart procedures up 25% in our attach rates. We're seeing similar dynamics in imaging, where our Precision suites' reagent packs grew 21% on higher scan volumes.

Second, product innovation pipeline: the launch of our Horizon R3 with integrated single-use FlexArm instruments—certified 510(k) cleared in March—has boosted consumables attach rates to 145% of capital revenue within the first six months post-placement, versus 120% historically. Additionally, our sustainability push with recyclable BioFlex kits has captured 15% market share in the $4.5 billion spinal implants segment, displacing multi-use competitors and driving 28% consumables growth there.

Third, pricing and mix discipline: we implemented modest 3-4% price increases on premium consumables in the US and EMEA, with no material pushback thanks to our clinical outcome data—our systems show 18% lower complication rates in ablation procedures versus legacy tech. Gross margins on consumables expanded 210 basis points to 82%, while capital held at 52%, lifting blended gross margin to 74%.

Regionally, the trends vary but reinforce the consumables tilt. US (62% of revenue): consumables mix at 78%, up from 74% YoY, propelled by 15% growth in ASCs. CMS reimbursement tailwinds under the 2024 OPPS final rule—adding $1,200+ per Horizon procedure—drove 20% utilization growth. We're gaining share versus Intuitive in robotics, with 35% of new ASC placements.

EMEA (18% of revenue): mix steady at 72%, with consumables up 16% on strong German and UK hospital capex cycles. Capital placements dipped 2% due to UK NHS budget scrutiny; we're mitigating with our leasing program, which converted 40% of deferred sales.

APAC ex-China (12% of revenue): highest growth at 25% for consumables, mix at 75%, led by Japan’s robotic surgery mandate expansion. Horizon placements doubled YoY to 45 units.

China (8% of revenue): capital-heavy at 45% mix due to NMPA approvals for Horizon R3 in Q1, but consumables ramped 30% post-launch. We've localized 60% of catheter production in Suzhou to de-risk geopolitical supply chain risks.

Strategically, we're doubling down on this mix for predictable cash flow—consumables now generate 85% of our operating cash flow, funding a $450 million R&D spend this year, including our stealth AI-driven autonomous imaging platform set for 2025 launch. Acquisitions like our $1.2 billion buyout of NeuroCath last year added $180 million in high-margin neurovascular consumables, instantly lifting mix by 2 points.

Looking forward, we expect the consumables mix to reach 77-78% by year-end, with FY24 guidance intact at 15-17% total revenue growth. Risks include potential hospital capex slowdowns from high interest rates, but our 18-month backlog of $3.2 billion—65% consumables-skewed—provides visibility. We're also monitoring GLP-1 drug impacts on bariatrics, but early data shows neutral effect on our ortho and cardio franchises.

In summary, our capital-consumables flywheel is spinning faster than ever, positioning us for sustained 20%+ EPS growth through the decade.

Then, overall performance highlights and key achievements. We delivered another outstanding quarter, underscoring the strength of our innovation-driven strategy amid a global medtech market growing at a solid 6.2% CAGR through 2028, per recent Grand View Research data. NovaMed is a leader in the medical devices space, with a diversified portfolio spanning cardiovascular interventions, orthopedic implants, neuromodulation, and our fast-growing robotics and digital health platforms.

Total revenue reached $1.28 billion, up 16% year-over-year on a reported basis and 17% on a constant currency basis. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, fueled by a mix of procedural volume recovery, market share gains, and the successful ramp of new product launches. Excluding COVID-related testing revenue from last year—which we deliberately exited to focus on high-margin chronic care segments—organic growth was an impressive 19%.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.62, surpassing our guidance midpoint by 8% and up 22% year-over-year. This was driven by disciplined margin expansion: gross margins expanded 320 basis points to 66.8%, thanks to favorable product mix—particularly our premium cardiovascular portfolio—and manufacturing efficiencies from our new Greenfield, Ireland facility, which is now running at 85% capacity utilization. Operating margins hit 28.4%, up from 25.1% last year, reflecting $45 million in cost savings from our Supply Chain Resilience Program, including localized sourcing of critical components like titanium alloys for orthopedics to mitigate ongoing geopolitical risks in rare earths.

Breaking it down by segment, our Cardiovascular business, our largest at 42% of revenue, grew 20% to $517 million. Key driver here was the continued adoption of our NovaFlow TAVR platform, which captured 14% U.S. market share in structural heart—closing the gap on leaders like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut. We implanted over 12,000 units globally, up 35% YoY, with strong evidence from our pivotal TRIUMPH trial showing 2.5% lower 30-day mortality versus competitors. In ablation therapies, our FlexPulse RF system for AFib treatment saw 25% procedure growth, bolstered by expanded reimbursement in Europe under the new DRG codes.

Orthopedics delivered 13% growth to $385 million, with standout performance in our robotic-assisted knee systems. The NovaKnee R1 platform, integrated with AI-driven preoperative planning akin to Stryker's Mako, achieved FDA 510(k) clearance for outpatient use in March, driving a 40% U.S. uptake surge. We also hit a milestone with 50,000 implants cumulatively, reducing revision rates by 18% per our post-market data.

Neuromodulation and Robotics rounded out the picture, up 22% combined to $378 million. Our NeuroStim dorsal column device for chronic pain now holds 22% share in the U.S. SCS market, competing head-on with Abbott's Proclaim, while our EndoBot single-port robotic platform notched first human cases in Asia-Pacific, with partnerships like the one with Singapore General Hospital paving the way for broader adoption.

Regionally, performance was balanced and resilient. The U.S., 55% of revenue, grew 18%, propelled by pent-up demand in elective procedures—now at 105% of pre-COVID volumes—and favorable CMS reimbursement for our portfolio under the 2024 OPPS final rule, which boosted ASPs by 4.2%. Europe, at 25% of revenue, expanded 14% constant currency, despite softer German hospital budgets; we offset this with 28% growth in the UK and France via our Horizon EU direct sales force, now covering 75% of top-tier cath labs. Asia-Pacific surged 25% to $210 million, led by China approvals for three products—including our TAVR valve via the NMPA fast-track—and a landmark distribution deal with Terumo for Japan. Emerging markets like India and Brazil contributed 8% growth, with volume-based pricing models helping penetrate high-growth ambulatory surgery centers.

Key achievements this quarter really set us apart in a competitive landscape. First, regulatory wins: we secured CE Mark for our AI-enhanced CardioVision imaging suite, which uses deep learning algorithms to improve lesion detection in coronary angiography by 32%—positioning us against Siemens Healthineers' Artis platform. This builds on our 2023 FDA Breakthrough Designation. Second, strategic M&A: we closed the $450 million acquisition of BioFlex Therapeutics, adding their bioresorbable stents to our pipeline and immediately accretive by $0.08 to EPS. Third, R&D momentum: we dosed the first patients in our Phase III trial for the NovaPulse neuromodulation system for hypertension, targeting the $15 billion renal denervation market post-ReCor and Medtronic's Symplicity Spyral approvals. And on sustainability, we achieved 25% reduction in Scope 3 emissions through recycled polymers in our orthopedic implants, aligning with EU MDR green procurement mandates.

Strategically, these results validate our 'Innovate, Penetrate, Expand' framework. We're leaning into megatrends like the aging population—projected to drive 7% annual U.S. ortho demand—and the shift to value-based care, where our connected devices ecosystem now integrates with Epic and Cerner EHRs for real-time outcomes data, improving payer negotiations. Supply chain-wise, we've derisked 95% of critical components with dual-sourcing post the 2023 resin shortages. Looking ahead, we're raising FY2024 guidance: revenue growth to 15-16%, adjusted EPS to $6.45-$6.60, with Q3 at $1.32-$1.35 billion.

Then, competitive dynamics and market share trends. The global medical devices market is projected to grow at a 5.2% CAGR through 2028, reaching approximately $650 billion, fueled by demographic tailwinds like aging populations, rising chronic disease prevalence, and the shift toward value-based care. Within this, our focus areas—cardiovascular interventions, orthopedics, and neuromodulation—represent a $180 billion total addressable market growing at 6.8% annually. But growth alone doesn't drive shareholder value; it's about capturing share in a highly fragmented, innovation-driven landscape.

In Q2, we expanded our global market share by 150 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% across our core franchises, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of share gains. This was driven by a 14% organic revenue increase in our highest-margin segments, outpacing the broader market's 7% procedure growth. Unit volumes grew 9%, while average selling prices held firm at +2% despite reimbursement headwinds, reflecting our premium positioning.

By franchise: Cardiovascular Interventions (52% of revenue) remains our growth engine, with structural heart and electrophysiology leading. In TAVR, we grew share from 18% to 21% globally, capturing 250bps from Edwards Lifesciences and Medtronic. Our NovaFlow TAVR platform, with its repositionable design and lower paravalvular leak rates (sub-1% in our PROVE-IT trial data), drove a 22% procedure increase in the U.S., where we now hold 28% share. Internationally, we're at 15% share, up from 11%, thanks to CE Mark expansions and partnerships in Japan and Australia. Edwards' Sapien 3 Ultra remains dominant in high-risk patients, but our lower-profile delivery system is winning in intermediate-risk cases.

In electrophysiology, we gained 300bps to 16% global share, propelled by our RhythmSync mapping system, which integrates AI-driven signal processing for 25% faster ablation times versus Biosense Webster's CARTO platform. Abbott's Advisor HD grids are a strong competitor, but our system's sub-millimeter accuracy and compatibility with single-shot pulsed-field ablation catheters positioned us to capture 12% of the $4.2 billion EP market.

Orthopedics (28% of revenue): share expanded 100bps to 9.8% in hips and knees, challenging Stryker and Zimmer Biomet. Our Triad Cementless Acetabular System, with its porous tantalum coating for 98% osseointegration at two years (per our ORTHO-TRACE registry), drove 11% U.S. knee procedure growth and 200bps share gain to 14%. In China, local players like United Orthopedic captured some share via lower-cost options, but we've countered with a 20% ASP premium in robotics-assisted procedures.

Neuromodulation (12% of revenue): we grew share 180bps to 11.2%, outpacing Medtronic's Intellis platform. Our NeuroPulse DBS system for Parkinson's, with adaptive closed-loop stimulation reducing battery life by 40%, gained 25% U.S. share in DBS procedures.

Regionally: U.S. (68% revenue) at 14.2% share, up 200bps. Europe (18%) flat at 10%, but UK/Benelux up. Asia-Pacific (10%) mixed, with Japan/Australia gains but China erosion to 4%. Emerging markets grew 25%.

Key competitive pressures: innovation race with Intuitive and J&J; we've invested $450 million in R&D for three 510(k) clearances. Supply chain stabilized margins at 68%. M&A like our NeuroStim tuck-in added share. Regulatory tailwinds from CMS IPPS.

We're reshaping dynamics through clinical differentiation. Our 2024 procedure growth guidance of 12-15% embeds 200bps share expansion.

Finally, impact of pricing and cost management initiatives, which were key drivers behind our Q2 gross margin expansion of 210 basis points to 68.2%, and our adjusted operating margin improvement of 320 basis points to 24.5%. These efforts not only offset persistent inflationary headwinds—particularly in specialized resins and titanium alloys used in our structural heart and neuromodulation portfolios—but also positioned us to deliver 8% organic revenue growth despite softer procedural volumes in orthopedics.

In the quarter, we realized a 4.2% increase in ASPs across our core franchises. This was driven by a disciplined contract renewal strategy with our top 20 U.S. IDNs like Kaiser Permanente and HCA Healthcare, which represent 45% of our U.S. med device revenue. We successfully passed through 2-3% escalators tied to CPI adjustments in 85% of these renewals, while introducing outcome-based pricing models for our next-generation TAVR portfolio. Under these contracts, pricing tiers are linked to 30-day readmission rates and one-year durability metrics, resulting in an effective ASP uplift of 6.1% for TAVR in the U.S.

In the U.S., where Medicare reimbursement for our peripheral intervention stents faced a 2.7% ASP cut under the CY2024 OPPS final rule, we mitigated this through mix shift—growing high-acuity procedures like our drug-eluting bioresorbable scaffolds by 15% YoY, which command 25-30% pricing premiums. In Europe, despite HTA scrutiny delaying reimbursement for our neuromodulation leads, we secured favorable pricing in 12 new markets via bundled payments emphasizing long-term cost savings from reduced opioid reliance. ASPs there rose 3.8%. Emerging markets saw modest 1.5% ASP pressure from local tenders, but volume growth of 22% compensated.

On cost management, we delivered $145 million in savings, on track for $550 million full-year. COGS savings of 65% from dual-sourcing high-purity polymers, long-term agreements with Dow and BASF, and lean Six Sigma yielding 12% scrap reduction in Galway. Cobots in Salt Lake City cut labor by 18%. SG&A savings of $52 million from Value360 platform reducing sales travel 25%, and R&D prioritization deferring $28 million in low-ROI projects.

These initiatives underscore our high-margin, outcomes-driven model, supported by 15 Level 1 RCTs. Our gross margin now trails Boston Scientific's by just 50 bps. Looking forward, pricing to contribute 3-4% to 2025 growth, costs to $650 million.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter. Revenue hit $1.28 billion, up 17% constant currency, with gross margins at 66.8% and operating margins at 28.4%. Adjusted EPS of $1.62 beat expectations. Our balance sheet remains solid with $2.8 billion in cash, supporting $450 million R&D and bolt-on M&A.
